note: Round-4 scout output (10 read-only Sonnet scouts over surfaces rounds 1-3 never covered: purchasing, supplier, part master, notifications/reorder, reporting, truck, equipment-compatibility, routing/app-shell, shared-utils, rules/data-model). Each dedup'd against register.json + round3-candidates.json. UNAPPROVED, awaiting Owner prioritization. Priority/track/liveness/verified are Claude's synthesis. TWO items reach into special tracks: 'tier2-rules' (fix requires a Firestore Rules change = Tier-2, separate workstream) and 'owner-decision' (production-enabled feature that always fails = product/config decision, not an auto-fix).
themes: STRUCTURAL gaps dominate this round vs round-3's localized defects: 'built+tested but never wired' (findActiveServiceGroupKey, Saved Reports), 'reads the dormant/wrong collection' (Operations procurement panel), 'production-enabled but mathematically always fails' (truck deactivate/delete)
safe-copy error convention still leaking on new surfaces (PartDetail 7 actions) — same class as #931/L
two authoritative-module latent bugs seeded for the finance program: allocateMoney negative-remainder + partMaster drops wholeUnit/equipmentModelId

candidates.problem: Operations dashboard Procurement panel reads the dormant Epic-5 `purchase_orders` collection (only writer is a demo seed script, never wired to a deployed callable), not the LIVE `reorder_purchase_orders` the Purchasing workspace uses.
candidates.impact: Operations dashboard permanently shows 'No purchase orders yet' in any real environment regardless of actual purchasing activity — a false 'no activity' signal.

candidates.problem: matchesFilter 'contains' case requires typeof raw === 'string', but list fields (tags, relationshipTypes) store arrays, so 'contains' — declared legal by the catalog/validator — never matches any row. containsAny handles arrays correctly; contains doesn't.
candidates.impact: A report filtering tags/relationshipTypes with 'contains' silently returns zero rows every time, no error, for an operator presented as legal.

candidates.problem: runReportDefinition picks a single outcome kind: droppedColumns>0 returns 'partially-authorized' even when truncated/widened are ALSO true. describeRunOutcome switches on kind and the 'partially-authorized' branch never reads outcome.truncated/rowCap, so truncation is dropped from the UI.
candidates.impact: A run that both drops a column AND hits a row/scan cap shows only 'Showing what you can view' with no truncation signal — a cut-off dataset mistaken for complete, silently undercounting decisions.

candidates.problem: PartDetail gates Request-Reorder on !reorderRequest, where useReorderRequestForPart returns the most-recent request regardless of status. Once it reaches any terminal status, reorderRequest stays truthy forever and the control never renders again. PartsList correctly scopes its equivalent to pendingRequests only.
candidates.impact: Any part that completes one reorder cycle (received/cancelled/voided/rejected) can never be reordered again via the Part Detail screen — a permanent dead end on the highest-traffic reorder entry point.

candidates.problem: useReorderRequestForPart's requestId branch onSnapshot error callback always sets error:'not_found', discarding the real code (permission-denied/unavailable), contradicting sibling hooks that preserve the error. PartDetail then renders 'could not be found' for any failure.
candidates.impact: A denied/transient failure on a ?requestId= reorder link shows a misleading 'could not be found' and withholds the whole reorder/PO/receive action surface under a false data-nonexistence pretext.

candidates.problem: Drawer only closes via NavLink onClick or the media-query flip; no useLocation-driven effect. Browser back/forward, <Navigate replace> redirects, and in-content <Link>s change route without closing the mobile drawer.
candidates.impact: On <900px, opening the drawer then using back/forward (or landing on a redirect, or tapping a dashboard card) leaves the full-screen overlay open on top of the new page, blocking content.

candidates.problem: Seven reorder-workflow handlers (assign, start purchasing, purchasing update, record PO, mark received, inventory action, request reorder) call setError(err.message) directly, bypassing workflowActionErrorMessage(err) that the same file's Approve/Reject already uses. Same class as the #931 sweep, new file.
candidates.impact: Parts Managers see raw Firestore/Rules error strings on 7 of ~9 write actions, inconsistent with the one action in the same file that does it correctly.

candidates.problem: findActiveServiceGroupKey is exported, documented as driving the active-group highlight, and unit-tested, but AppRail never imports/calls it (zero consumers). The group div has no active styling hook.
candidates.impact: The 'which group is the current route in' affordance was designed and validated but never connected — no group-level orientation in the multi-item Service hierarchy. Passing tests mask a disconnected feature.

candidates.problem: changeStatus accepts any TRUCK_STATUSES value incl OUT_OF_SERVICE, with no inventory-presence check and no active-flag change — bypassing the governed deactivateTruck path (which requires inventory ABSENT and sets active=false). isTruckStatus doesn't exclude OUT_OF_SERVICE.
candidates.impact: Any admin/dispatcher can force status=OUT_OF_SERVICE while active stays true and inventory presence is never checked — a truck simultaneously 'deactivated' by status and 'active' by flag, circumventing the feature's one safety rail. (Fix = exclude OUT_OF_SERVICE from changeStatus; repo-only.)

candidates.problem: types/validation/commands define, validate, and FK-check Part.wholeUnit/equipmentModelId, but partToFirestore never writes them and partFromFirestore never reads them back (grep: zero references in the repository).
candidates.impact: createPart/updatePart with wholeUnit+equipmentModelId passes validation + FK check, appears to succeed, but the classification/link is never stored and reverts to undefined on next read — the whole-unit<->serialized-equipment linkage the spec exists to carry is silently lost.

candidates.problem: createPurchaseOrder only sums line items — no non-empty check, no per-item quantity>0 / unitPrice>=0 check. Accepts items:[] (total 0) or negative qty/price (negative total). The modern governed supplier-item validator enforces exactly these; this legacy writer has none.
candidates.impact: Once wired to a callable/UI, a malformed request creates a zero/negative-cost PO with no validation error, corrupting downstream totals/reporting. Latent (unexported today).

candidates.problem: allocateMoney's remainder loop guard is `remainder > 0`; for a negative Money value the leftover remainder is negative so the loop never runs and a minor unit is dropped. Verified: allocateMoney(money(-1000,'USD'),[1,1,1]) sums to -999 not -1000, breaking the module's exact-sum guarantee.
candidates.impact: Any future prorating of a negative Money value (refund/credit/discount split) silently loses minor units. Latent (zero callers) but in the authoritative Money module finance builds on; negative path untested.

candidates.problem: importCompatibilitySource runs listByCompatibilityId (unbounded, no .limit()) inside its write transaction to conflict-analyze the full immutable evidence set — no per-relationship write-time cap, unlike the read path's MAX_EVIDENCE_PER_RELATIONSHIP.
candidates.impact: As evidence accumulates for a heavily-cited relationship, transaction read/latency/size grow unboundedly until timeout — then every future import for that relationship fails permanently. Latent (compatibility active:false).

candidates.problem: The scroll-active-item-into-view effect depends on [activeDomainPath] only, so switching items within the same expanded domain never fires it.
candidates.impact: In long domains (Inventory 8, Administration 9) at short rail height, clicking down the list selects an item that stays off-screen — the exact defect the effect was added to fix, for the in-domain case.

candidates.problem: setDriver only checks isEmployeeActive; no query for another truck already carrying the same assignedDriverEmployeeId, and the repository exposes no such lookup.
candidates.impact: The same employee can be the assigned driver on multiple trucks with no detection, producing an untrustworthy 1:1-presented driver roster.

candidates.problem: The builder renders every legal comparator (in/between/containsAny) in the operator select but the value control is always a single scalar. Picking an array comparator makes validation permanently fail (requires non-empty array), so Run stays disabled with no way to fix.
candidates.impact: Three declared comparators are selectable but dead ends — 'Tags contains any of…' / 'Created between…' hit an unresolvable error.

candidates.problem: SavedReports.onNew always persists a hardcoded starterDefinition stub; ReportBuilder has no Save control; Open never hydrates ReportBuilder ('Editing and running reports isn't available yet.').
candidates.impact: Saved Reports (fully governed backend) has no connection to the one screen that builds a report — can't save what you built or run what you saved; every 'New' litters the list with identical stubs.

candidates.problem: deactivateTruckCallable runs with the default UNKNOWN_INVENTORY predicate (EI serialized-asset/ledger-at-location persistence doesn't exist yet), so deactivateTruck always throws InventoryStateUnknownError. With TRUCK_MANAGEMENT_WRITE_READY=true for production, the 'Confirm deactivate' button is fully enabled and reachable but every invocation is guaranteed to fail.
candidates.impact: A production-enabled write path that can never succeed. DECISION NEEDED: gate the UI off in prod (config/UI) OR build the governed inventory-presence source. Not an auto-fix.

candidates.problem: All 11 REFERENCE_AUTHORITIES are wrapped in unverifiable() (always UNKNOWN); deleteTruckCreatedInError throws ReferenceStateUnknownError whenever refs !== CLEAR. The admin 'Delete truck (created in error)' control is enabled in production (writeReady) but always rejected.
candidates.impact: A destructive admin feature shipped enabled in production, mathematically guaranteed to fail until truck-indexed operational-history persistence exists across all 11 authorities. DECISION NEEDED (same as deactivate): gate off in prod OR build the persistence.

candidates.problem: match /locations/{locationId} allows create/update for any admin/dispatcher with zero field validation (no key allowlist, no accountId type/immutability check) unlike accounts/equipment/reorder_requests. equipmentLocationBelongsToAccount trusts locations.accountId at equipment-create time, but locations.accountId is never pinned immutable or re-validated.
candidates.impact: A location's accountId can be changed after equipment validated against the old value, permanently diverging equipment.accountId from locations.accountId with no detection. FIX REQUIRES A FIRESTORE RULES CHANGE = Tier-2, route to a rules-authoring workstream.

candidates.problem: match /inventory_actions/{actionId} allow create is just isAdminOrDispatcher() with no key allowlist/type/required-field checks, despite a comment claiming parity with reorder_requests (which enforces a 35-key canonical schema). Validation lives only in a client domain helper Rules can't enforce is the caller.
candidates.impact: This append-only audit trail for human inventory adjustments can receive malformed/incomplete docs from any admin/dispatcher path bypassing the client helper, corrupting the trusted history with nothing in Rules to catch it. FIX REQUIRES A FIRESTORE RULES CHANGE = Tier-2.
